{{Short description|Performing  source coding and channel coding in a single operation}}
{{distinguish|Joint encoding}}
In [[information theory]], '''joint source–channel coding''' is the encoding of a redundant [[Information source (mathematics)|information source]] for transmission over a [[noisy channel]], and the corresponding [[Code|decoding]], using a single code instead of the more conventional steps of [[source coding]] followed by [[channel coding]].

Joint source–channel coding has been proposed and implemented for a variety of situations, including speech and videotransmission.<ref>{{cite book |author1=M. R. Soleymani |author2=A. K. Khandani |name-list-style=amp |year=1991 |chapter=Vector Trellis Quantization for Noisy Channels |editor1=Bishnu S. Sicuranza |editor2=Sanjit K. Mitra |title=Multidimensional processing of video signals |publisher=Springer |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=H-6XpIRNDGAC&q=%22joint+source+channel+coding%22+date:0-1992&pg=PT65 |isbn=0-7923-9228-0 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4615-3616-1_4|url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/33907/files/UzV92.pdf }}</ref>
